newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - Saudis said to see OPEC set to roll over.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Saudis said to see OPEC set to roll over.

text.p: Saudi Arabia thinks the likely decision at Vienna talks of a divided OPEC oil cartel this week will be a six-month "roll over" of current output quotas, in the hope that seasonal demand for fuel will retrieve prices.

Gulf sources relayed signals from the delegation of Saudi Arabia, linchpin of the 11-nation cartel, on the eve of a ministerial conference of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries which begins on Wednesday.
"All options are open but the most likely outcome is a roll over for six months (from June 30)," said one Gulf source.
The Saudis also want a commitment to better quota discipline but delegates say that it is hard to see how OPEC can begin to police that.
Industry monitors calculate that actual volume exceeds the mandated ceiling of 25.03 million barrels daily by as much as two million - some 800,000 from just one country, Venezuela.
Petroleos de Venezuela, its state oil company, has said that OPEC ought to abandon quotas altogether and opt for a policy of expanding its share of the world market.
The Venezuelan minister, Erwin Arrieta, said he would not actually advocate that at this week's OPEC session, but that he would like to air ideas for change.
Others in OPEC, among them Iran, blame the violators for the way that benchmark prices are back around $18 per barrel after a rally late in 1996 as high as $25.
Low oil company stocks and a cold northern winter helped that rally, and the Saudis apparently count on seasonal factors to succour OPEC once again.
"The market is right now healthy," said a Gulf source. "You cannot be certain but the most likely case is that prices will improve in the third quarter".
This source said that although there had been a build up in stocks, these were still lower than last year in terms of forward days cover of global demand.

The OPEC pre-conference ritual unfolded at its customary leisured pace on Tuesday. The secretariat pencilled in 1300 GMT on Tuesday afternoon for a session of what it calls its quota compliance committee.
This comprises Iran,Indonesia and Nigeria. Nigeria, monitors say, is another cash-pinched Third World seller that is exceeding its quota.
Gulf Arab OPEC oil ministers - of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar - also planned an informal meeting of their own during Tuesday, Gulf sources have said.
Crude oil futures prices ticked higher, with London August North Sea Brent Blend advancing above $18 per barrel for a gain of more than 30 cents since early Monday.
But traders said that OPEC was less a factor than renewed tensions between Iraq and the United Nations.

They cited a continuing delay on further Iraqi oil sales under a U.N.-supervised oil-for-food deal that partially relaxes Gulf War sanctions. Oil Minister Amir Rasheed of Iraq was not due in Vienna until late on Tuesday evening.
